speaker: Doctor
text:
It seems the severity of your pain fluctuates with bowel movements, which is a significant clue. Have you noticed any changes in your stool's frequency, consistency, or color, and have you traveled to areas with different water supplies recently?

REQUEST TEST: Stool_Ova_and_Parasites and Stool_Culture.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those normal stool results effectively rule out infectious causes like parasites or bacteria. Given the pain relief after bowel movements and the chronic nature of your symptoms, I suspect this may be Inflammatory Bowel Disease or Irritable Bowel Syndrome. Have you noticed any nighttime symptoms that wake you from sleep, or any joint pain or skin rashes elsewhere? REQUEST TEST: C-Reactive Protein (CRP) and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR).

speaker: Doctor
text: The ESR of 10 mm/hr is within the normal range, which makes systemic inflammation like Crohn's or Ulcerative Colitis less likely. Does your abdominal pain specifically localize to the right lower quadrant, and have you ever noticed small, non-healing bumps (erythema nodosum) on your shins or tender lumps (sacroiliitis) in your hips? REQUEST TEST: Fecal Calprotectin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
With normal inflammatory markers and no evidence of infection or active inflammation, I am leaning towards a functional disorder like Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). Have you noticed any relationship between your symptoms and specific foods, such as dairy, gluten, or high-fat meals? Also, have you been under significant stress lately?

REQUEST TEST: Food_Allergy_Panel and Lactose_Intolerance_Test.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
